retention_decision.data_provenance_note: The main 101-item diagnostic run (scripts/p10.1.1-hierarchical-diagnostic.mjs) measured search_eligible_chunks for all configs but did not separately capture dense_latency_p50_ms/peak_rss_bytes for the Hierarchical-1024 configs (C/D), an implementation gap discovered after that run completed. Rather than change the pinned decision rule (hierarchical-retention-rule.mjs, unmodified) to work around missing inputs, a bounded 10-item companion run (scripts/p10.1.1-determinism-and-latency-check.mjs, real local BGE-M3, same fixed prefix sample used for the determinism check) supplied the missing latency/RSS figures under the SAME rule. This is completing the rule's required inputs, not altering the rule or its thresholds after seeing the recall result.

empirical_note_leaf_pool_vs_full_pool: In this real corpus, D's leaf-only candidate pool was set-identical to C's full search-eligible pool for 101/101 items -- domain/chunking/chunker.mjs's own retrieval_eligible rule already excludes SECTION_PARENT/EVENT_PARENT/HOLDING_STATUS_PARENT/TABLE_WHOLE from the searchable index for these documents, so parent-role chunks were never actually competing for top-k slots even in C's "raw-flat" treatment. Any C-vs-D difference in this Turn's results therefore comes from the sibling-collapse + document-diversity-cap step alone, not from candidate-pool composition.
